_about: Siracusa-Sicilia, 10 Oct 2026 — GOLD6 §8 readings. Every fact comes from the guide's own cards and venue records (venues checked 4 Oct 2026, hours seen 4–5 Oct 2026, the hot board checked 5 Oct 2026).

onenight.title: Une nuit
onenight.kicker: One night ashore · Ortigia on foot, or one baroque town by car · walking order
onenight.lede: On Ortigia the evening is all on foot: a glass as the sun drops over the Porto Grande, dinner, then cocktails from about nine. The baroque towns are a drive, so pick one and make it the whole night. Each plan below is one evening, in the order you walk it; every name opens its full card. Where the guide has no hours for a place, the step says so.
onenight.door_en: Crew ashore for one evening: a plan for each quarter — Ortigia on foot, or one baroque town by car; the glass, the table, the bar, the late granita.
onenight.door_note: Le coucher du soleil · la petite table · le bar · la granita

quarters.name: Ortigia north · the bridge to the Temple of Apollo
quarters.line: The harbour from a roof, the classic room under tufa vaults, the island's best drink.

steps.name: Grand Hotel Ortigia, La Terrazza
steps.text: The roof on Viale Mazzini, across the Porto Grande from the Ortigia waterfront: a spritz or a local spumante as the anchorage goes gold. Call +39 0931 464600 first: non-guest access is not stated on its site.

steps.name: Don Camillo
steps.text: Walk over the bridge to Via Maestranza 96 and Giovanni Guarnieri's room, his since 1985: the spaghetti delle Sirene, prawns and sea urchin, and save room for dessert. Listed, no longer starred. The guide has no hours for it: book ahead on +39 0931 67133.

steps.name: Barcollo
steps.text: Piazza Cesare Battisti, in the open by the Temple of Apollo: a signature cocktail and chef Davide Cucuzza's tapas, from about 21:00. Last confirmed in 2025: check it is trading before you walk over.

quarters.after: Instead of the roof: a glass of natural Sicilian wine at the counter of [[card:Enoteca Solaria|Enoteca Solaria]] on Via Roma, from 19:00 (its 2026 trading is not confirmed on an own site). Cheaper: [[venue:latteria-mamma-iabica|Latteria Mamma Iabica]], just off the island on Via G.B. Perasso, Slow Food's Chiocciola for 2026 — the guide has no hours for it, so look in first.

quarters.name: Ortigia west · the Fonte Aretusa and Piazza Duomo
quarters.line: The spring at sunset, dinner facing a Greek temple, the square after dark.

steps.name: Fonte Aretusa
steps.text: The spring faces west over the Porto Grande: fresh water a few steps above the harbour, papyrus growing wild in the pool. Free, seen from the street at any hour.

steps.name: Regina Lucia
steps.text: Piazza Duomo 6, tables facing the Doric columns built into the cathedral front. Classic Sicilian dishes with a creative turn; don't skip dessert. Wed–Mon 12:00–23:00, closed Tuesday; online dinner slots to 21:30, later by phone on +39 0931 22509.

steps.name: Piazza Duomo, after dinner
steps.text: Walk out to the middle of the oval: the cathedral, Palazzo Vermexio, Palazzo Beneventano and Santa Lucia alla Badia, all of it Iblei limestone, lit after dark. Always open.

quarters.after: Spend more: walk south to the island's tip for [[venue:cortile-spirito-santo|Cortile Spirito Santo]], Via Salomone 21, Siracusa's first MICHELIN star — tasting menus €110–160 (Gambero Rosso, June 2025); book.

quarters.name: Noto · the Corso at dusk
quarters.line: About 40 minutes by car: gold stone at dusk, a starred dinner up the hill, almond granita to finish.

steps.name: Palazzo Nicolaci
steps.text: Via Corrado Nicolaci at dusk, when the lions, sirens and winged horses under the balconies are lit from the side. Inside until 19:00 Monday to Saturday; on Sunday it shuts at 18:00.

steps.name: Crocifisso
steps.text: Up the hill to Via Principe Umberto 46 and Marco Baglieri's one-star: artichoke two ways on brioche with anchovy sauce, cod with leek foam and cuttlefish ink. Dinner service, closed Wednesdays; book.

steps.name: Caffè Sicilia
steps.text: Back down to the Corso for an almond granita at Corrado Assenza's counter. Its own site gives two sets of closing hours, 22:30 or 23:00 on weekdays: ring before you walk down.

quarters.after: Whoever drives back to Siracusa skips the wine. Park below Porta Reale, as the [[card:Noto: a city moved and rebuilt|Noto card]] says.

quarters.name: Marzamemi · the tonnara square
quarters.line: About 50 minutes by car: the old tuna-fishery square at dusk, then fish.

steps.name: Piazza Regina Margherita
steps.text: The courtyard of the old tonnara, now the village square, the sea on three sides. Buy a vacuum-packed bar of [[card:Marzamemi tuna: bottarga, ventresca, mosciame|bottarga]] in the village shops while they are open.

steps.name: Taverna La Cialoma
steps.text: Inside the old tuna-fishery buildings on the piazza, a sea terrace behind: the day's fish, simply cooked. The guide has no hours for it: book ahead on +39 0931 841772.

quarters.after: Dressier: [[venue:cortile-arabo|Cortile Arabo]], on its terrace over the rocks in Vicolo Villadorata. The bottarga busiate at [[venue:campisi|Campisi]] is the other reason to come, but its restaurant season is not confirmed for October 2026.

quarters.name: Ragusa Ibla · the two-star on the spur
quarters.line: About 1 hour 20 by car, for one table: the night is the meal.

steps.name: Down the steps into Ibla
steps.text: Walk down the steps from upper Ragusa to the old town on its spur, quiet, steep and small.

steps.name: Duomo
steps.text: Ciccio Sultano's two stars beside the cathedral of San Giorgio: 'Stupor Mundi', eight courses, or à la carte. The rooms are small and it is expensive; book well ahead on +39 0932 651265.

quarters.after: This is the only table we list in Ibla, and no bar: eat, then drive back.

quarters.name: Modica · the chocolate town
quarters.line: About 1 hour 10 by car: the stairs to San Giorgio, then a starred chef's trattoria.

steps.name: The stairs up to San Giorgio
steps.text: Modica fills two ravines with baroque churches and staircases: climb to San Giorgio before dark.

steps.name: Radici
steps.text: Via Grimaldi 55: Accursio Craparo gave up his star to cook generous traditional dishes here. Ask whether the old 'Spremuta di Sicilia' pasta survives. The guide has no hours for it: ring +39 331 236 9404.

quarters.after: Instead: [[venue:dabbanna|Dabbanna]] on Piazza Principe di Napoli, the grandchildren of a 1971 rotisserie and a ceviche called 'Ciauru ri mari'. Eat first, in the afternoon: a cremolata at [[venue:rosy-bar|Rosy Bar]] and a cinnamon bar at [[venue:antica-dolceria-bonajuto|Bonajuto]]; we have no evening hours for either.

getaway.title: Le week-end
getaway.door_en: Friday night to Sunday afternoon: the spring at sunset, the market before nine, the Greek theatre in the last light, almond granita in Noto and a cove you walk to.
getaway.door_note: La source · le marché · le théâtre · la granita
getaway.kicker: The getaway weekend · Friday night to Sunday afternoon
getaway.lede: Ortigia sells itself on the piazza at night, and the piazza is worth it. The rest of the weekend starts earlier: the market before nine, Doric columns lining a cathedral nave, the Greek theatre in its last ninety minutes of light, the harbour from a roof at sunset. On Sunday drive south for almond granita in Noto at opening and a cove in Vendicari you can only reach on foot, then fish in the tuna village. Every stop below is already in this guide and was checked in October 2026; where a card says unverified, so does the stop. This reading puts them in order, and tells you what to book before you fly.
book: [[venue:cortile-spirito-santo|Cortile Spirito Santo]] — for Saturday dinner: +39 0931 181 5404, booking recommended.
[[venue:don-camillo|Don Camillo]] — for Friday dinner: book ahead, +39 0931 67133.
[[venue:grand-hotel-ortigia|Grand Hotel Ortigia, La Terrazza]] — call +39 0931 464600 to ask whether non-guests can come up for the sunset aperitivo.
[[venue:taverna-la-cialoma|Taverna La Cialoma]] — for Sunday lunch: book ahead, +39 0931 841772, and confirm they serve lunch.
[[card:The Miqwe of Via Alagona|The Miqwe]] — guided tours only: call +39 0931 22255 for Saturday's times.

days.label: Friday
days.title: The spring, the vaults, the temple

stops.name: The Fonte Aretusa at sunset
stops.text: Leave the bags and walk to the western waterfront. At the balustrade, fresh water rises a few metres from the salt, with fish, ducks and wild papyrus in the pool; Ovid has the nymph [[card:Arethusa and Alpheus|Arethusa]] run under the sea from Greece to surface here. The Fonte faces west, so the sun goes down over the Porto Grande in front of you.
stops.meta: Largo Aretusa · free, from the street at any hour · no bread for the ducks

stops.name: Dinner at Don Camillo
stops.text: Ortigia's long-running serious room, under old tufa walls on Via Maestranza near the cathedral. It held a star for years and is listed, not starred, in MICHELIN 2026. Order the spaghetti delle Sirene with prawns and sea urchin, and save room for dessert.
stops.meta: Via Maestranza 96 · €€€ · book ahead, +39 0931 67133 · hours not in this guide

stops.name: A cocktail by the Temple of Apollo
stops.text: Walk north to Barcollo, now in a small open piazza by the Temple of Apollo. The drinks are by Andrea Franzò and Andrea Germiglio, the tapas by Davide Cucuzza, from MICHELIN-starred kitchens: real cooking, if dinner was light.
stops.meta: Piazza Cesare Battisti 6/8 · from about 21:00 · €€ · last confirmed 2025: check it is trading

stops.name: The Ortigia market, before nine
stops.text: Swordfish on ice and men calling prices along Via Emanuele de Benedictis, from the Temple of Apollo. The swordfish and red prawns go first. At the far end, [[venue:caseificio-borderi|Borderi]] builds its panino in front of you with the house ricotta and mozzarella: go before 10:30, and know that its hours and prices come from secondary sources only.
stops.meta: Via Emanuele de Benedictis · Mon–Sat about 7:00 until 14:00 (reported) · closed Sunday

stops.name: A temple inside the cathedral
stops.ref: card:Duomo di Siracusa: a temple still standing inside a church
stops.text: Walk round to Via Minerva first and see the Greek columns sticking out of the outer wall, then go in and down the left aisle between Doric shafts raised in the 5th century BC. On the corner of Palazzo Vermexio, look up at the cornice for [[card:Vermexio's lizard|the architect's lizard]].
stops.meta: Piazza Duomo · Oct–Apr 9:00–17:30, no tourist visits on Sunday · EUR 2 + EUR 1 booking fee (seen Oct 2026)

stops.name: Fifty-eight steps down to the Miqwe
stops.text: In the old Giudecca, a stair cut in the rock leads 18 metres down to a vaulted Jewish ritual bath still filled by spring water, sealed before the expulsion of 1492 and found again in 1989. Short, humid, unforgettable. Walk Via della Giudecca afterwards, past the puppet theatre of the [[card:★ Opera dei Pupi in Ortigia: the Vaccaro-Mauceri family|Vaccaro-Mauceri family]].
stops.meta: Via Alagona 52 · guided tours about every half hour, 11:00–17:00 (reported) · about EUR 5 (reported) · not accessible for reduced mobility

stops.name: Lunch at a seat in the market
stops.text: Back to the market for La Salumeria of Fratelli Burgio, conserve-makers since 1978: sit among the fish stalls for a tagliere of Piacentino ennese with saffron, pecorino with Bronte pistachio and filuneddu with caponata. The shelves around you hold the conserves and bottarga to take home.
stops.meta: Ortigia market (Piazza Cesare Battisti 4, reported) · closes about 15:30 · boards about €12–20 (Dissapore) · no booking

stops.name: The Greek theatre in the last light
stops.text: Across the bridges to the Neapolis, about 10 minutes by car or 25 on foot. Climb to the top row of the cavea, where Greek aqueduct water still trickles down the Nymphaeum, and look over the stage to the harbour. Then the [[card:The Ear of Dionysius|Ear of Dionysius]] in the quarry below: speak softly at the back of the cave and hear it come out as a shout.
stops.meta: Via del Teatro Greco · daily 9:00 to one hour before sunset · EUR 10 (seen Oct 2026), the Ear on the same ticket

stops.name: The Porto Grande from the roof
stops.text: On the way back, the roof terrace of the Grand Hotel Ortigia on Viale Mazzini: a spritz or a local spumante while the anchorage, the marina and the whole western side of the island turn gold.
stops.meta: Viale Mazzini · €€€ · call +39 0931 464600: non-guest access not stated

stops.name: Dinner at Cortile Spirito Santo
stops.text: Walk the length of the island to its southern tip. Giuseppe Torrisi spent three years at Bernard Loiseau's La Côte d'Or, and in late 2023 won the first MICHELIN star Siracusa ever had. The dinner of the trip: the 'scacciata' turned into ravioli, monkfish meunière with wild fennel, and the 'Assoluto di mandorla', an almond dessert moulded in the shape of Sicily.
stops.meta: Via Salomone 21 · tasting menus €110–160 (Gambero Rosso, June 2025) · booking recommended, +39 0931 181 5404

stops.name: Piazza Duomo, lit
stops.text: Walk back up to the oval square laid over the acropolis of the first Greek city, the cathedral on one side and Santa Lucia alla Badia closing the far end, and stand in the middle: 2,700 years of the city in one turn.

days.label: Sunday
days.title: Almond, gold stone, a cove, the tuna village

stops.name: Almond granita at Caffè Sicilia
stops.text: Drive south, about 40 minutes, and park below Porta Reale in Noto. On the Corso, Corrado Assenza's café, open since 1892, makes its granita from Noto almonds: have it with a brioche, then the strangest seasonal flavour on the board.
stops.meta: Corso Vittorio Emanuele 125, Noto · from 8:00 daily (its own site gives two sets of closing hours, seen 4 Oct 2026) · €–€€ · no booking

stops.name: The balconies of Palazzo Nicolaci
stops.text: Up Via Corrado Nicolaci to the balconies carried on lions, sirens and grimacing masks, then inside to the stucco stair and the ballroom with Apollo's chariot on the ceiling. Climb the [[card:Noto: a city moved and rebuilt|San Carlo bell tower]] for the roofs of the Corso (a small fee; the guide has no hours for it).
stops.meta: Via Corrado Nicolaci 20 · Sun 10:00–13:00, 14:30–18:00 (italia.it, seen Oct 2026) · small paid entry

stops.name: Vendicari, and the cove you walk to
stops.text: South on the SP19 to the reserve. Flamingos stop on the Pantano Grande in autumn, and a tonnara shell stands on the main beach. Calamosche, between two headlands, is about twenty minutes on foot from its gate, so it is never as full as the beaches you can drive to; in October the water is still warm.
stops.meta: SP19 Noto–Pachino, Calamosche gate · EUR 3.50, card payment only (reported Jul 2026) · gates 7:00–19:30 until 31 Oct (reported) · bring water: no services inside

stops.name: Fish in the tonnara square
stops.text: On to Marzamemi and Taverna La Cialoma, inside the old tuna-fishery buildings on Piazza Regina Margherita, named for the work-song the crews sang hauling the nets. The day's fish, simply cooked. Buy a bar of [[card:Marzamemi tuna: bottarga, ventresca, mosciame|bottarga]] in the village before you drive back, about 50 minutes to Siracusa.
stops.meta: Piazza Regina Margherita 23, Marzamemi · €€ · book ahead, +39 0931 841772 · hours not in this guide: confirm lunch

more.title: If you have only one evening
more.text: The [[card:Fonte Aretusa and its papyrus|Fonte Aretusa]] at sunset, dinner on Piazza Duomo at [[venue:regina-lucia|Regina Lucia]] facing the temple columns (closed Tuesday), then a cocktail at [[card:Barcollo|Barcollo]] by the Temple of Apollo. All of it on foot, inside one kilometre.

more.title: The grand night instead
more.text: Swap Saturday's dinner for [[venue:duomo|Duomo]] in Ragusa Ibla, Ciccio Sultano's two stars and Gambero Rosso's top Sicilian score for 2026: the 'Stupor Mundi' menu, eight courses, about 1 hour 20 by car each way. Small rooms, expensive; book well ahead. Nearer, [[venue:crocifisso|Crocifisso]] in Noto has one star and dinner service only; closed Wednesdays.

more.title: Or a night at the theatre
more.text: The Greek theatre is the signature evening of this coast, but not in autumn: the [[card:INDA: Greek tragedy where it was first played|INDA season]] plays Greek drama in the rock theatre from 7 May 2027, as the sun sets behind the stage. Book the cheap unnumbered upper seats and bring a cushion. In autumn the knights are at the [[card:★ Opera dei Pupi in Ortigia: the Vaccaro-Mauceri family|Opera dei Pupi]] on Via della Giudecca instead: phone +39 0931 465540 for show days.

more.title: This October
items: [[card:INDA 2027 tickets are on sale|INDA 2027 tickets]] have been on sale since 1 September: the upper cavea goes first for June weekends.
[[card:Regina Lucia — the last-minute table|Regina Lucia]] is open Wednesday to Monday, 12:00 to 23:00 (own site, 5 October): the first call when a booking falls through.
The [[card:The Grand Hotel's rooftop|Grand Hotel's rooftop]] serves dinner 19:30–22:30 (hotel site, 5 October); call first, non-guest access is not stated.
[[card:The puppets of San Martino|The puppets of San Martino]] fill Ortigia around 11 November; the 2026 programme was not published on 4 October: phone the theatre in late October.

Around 25–26 October sunlight through the rose window falls on [[card:Caravaggio's Burial of Saint Lucy|Caravaggio's Burial of Saint Lucy]] in Santa Lucia al Sepolcro, in the Borgata: open when the church is open, so check on the day.
Vendicari's gates are reported open 7:00–19:30 until 31 October, then 9:30–16:00: after that, do the cove before lunch.

more.title: Where to sleep
more.text: We have judged these places for a drink or a dinner, not for a night: we have not priced or stayed in the rooms. The [[card:Ortigia|Ortigia card]] says sleep on the island, where everything is on foot; if your hotel is inside the limited-traffic zone, have it register your plate before you arrive. The only hotel in this guide is the [[venue:grand-hotel-ortigia|Grand Hotel Ortigia]], on Viale Mazzini facing the Porto Grande. Out in the Vittoria vineyards, [[venue:arianna-occhipinti|Arianna Occhipinti]]'s farm has rooms.

more.title: What we would leave out
more.text: Driving into Ortigia: it is a camera-policed limited-traffic zone and the fine reaches you months later through the rental firm — park at the Talete and walk in ([[card:Driving into Ortigia and Taormina|the warning]]). The 'papyrus' paintings in Ortigia's shops, mostly banana-leaf paper: hold a sheet to the light and look for crossed strips. The drive up to the Castello Eurialo: [[card:The greatest of the Greek cities|shut for lack of staff since June 2024]] (La Sicilia, 9 July 2026). And the signposted [[card:The tomb that isn't Archimedes'|Tomb of Archimedes]], which is Roman.
